the 60 (Cadrane) — desk dial
DRAWING

AS SHOWN

Projected from docs/v15/the60_v15_assembly.step by hidden-line projection, with dimension text written from docs/v15/the60_v15/src/params.py. No hand drafting. The knob is drawn on its turned profile: the knurl is on the part but is not drawn.
MODELLED, NOT MADE — no v15 part has been produced. Dimensions are model values, not inspection results. Bodies tagged ENVELOPE or ASSUMED in the model are drawn as envelopes, not as the real part.
SECTION C-C scale 1.35 : 1
On the 90 deg - 270 deg axis, clutch ENGAGED. Right of the centreline is the motor at 90 deg; the servo's inboard end crosses the centreline.
CL
r 65.70 motor axis
r 83.20 bore
14.00 motor
4.20 carriage
8.80 band
NOTES
The drive is friction, not gears: a Ø35 motor bell running on the Ø166
bore through a 0.60 flat silicone band. Ratio 4.75 : 1. The gimbal drive
and its over-centre clutch went at v9 and have not come back.
JD-Power MY-3514C (2804), dia 35 x 14, on a carriage that slides radially
in a stadium hole through the aluminium core. The carriage shoe is dia 37
on the pad, so the motor's base face is at z 4.2 and its top at z 18.2.
The clutch IS the servo. An AGFRC C1.5CLS PRO linear servo (21.4 × 15.2 ×
6 envelope) pushes the carriage tab directly; 2.40 of travel takes the
bell from contact to 2.40 clear. Preload — 2.4 N nominal — is a servo
position set in software, not a spring.
Commutation: an MT6701 on a 12 x 12 board inside the carriage, under the
motor, reading a Ø6 × 2.5 diametric magnet in the shaft's lower end
through a dia 9 sight hole. Which end of the shaft carries the magnet is
ASSUMED. If it is the top, this board moves and the display rises about 3
mm, against 35.9 as modelled.
Not drawn, because nothing published says: the motor's bolt pattern (the
carriage has a Ø35.6 locating rim only), the servo's mounting lugs, and
the pushrod-to-tab joint. Measure all three on the real parts before
printing the carriage or the servo mount.
Band grip at 2.4 N is untested. If it slips under a firm hand, the
fallback is a 2 : 1 bell-crank between the servo and the tab — that
doubles the force and halves the travel, so the stadium hole would grow.
ENGAGED
0.60 band
RELEASED
DETAIL R - THE CLUTCH 4 : 1
Same section, same scale, 2.40 apart. Engaged, the band is squeezed 0.60 between
bell and bore. Released, the bell stands 2.40 clear and the knob free-spins.
The knob is never released by the wheels — only by the drive.
PLAN AT z 2.5 - INSIDE THE CORE scale 0.55 : 1
carriage shoe on the pad
servo tray screws
port face
The stadium hole is the two carriage positions plus the slot
between them: dia 38.5 wide, r 44.1 - 85.0 at 90 deg, with a 10 x 10 tab slot reaching in to r 39.7.
The carriage rides on the pad, not on the core. This cut is inside the cooling duct - see D05.
PLAN AT z 13.4 - THE DRIVE BAND scale 0.55 : 1
Contact is a line at 90 deg, at r 83.20. Everything else on this level -
motion board at 51 deg, speaker, servo tray - stays outside the bell.
The wall relief is cut for the bell, 2.0 a side; the base below z 8.5 is narrower.
CARRIAGE AND SERVO TRAY - ISOMETRIC 1.9 : 1
The two printed parts of the drive, with the commutation board in its pocket. Motor and servo are left off: their envelopes hide everything that has to be made.
Assembly: board into the carriage, motor on top, band over the bell, servo into the tray, tray on the plate, then set the preload in software.
